corruption

/kuh-RUP-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Corruption means dishonest or illegal behavior by people in positions of power, especially bribery or the abuse of entrusted authority for private gain.

The city audit exposed corruption in the housing office, where clerks had been approving permits in exchange for cash.

Example

The port shut down for a week after investigators found corruption among customs inspectors who had been waving smugglers' crates through for a share of the profits.

The inspectors traded the power of their official position for secret personal payment — that abuse of entrusted authority for private gain is the defining pattern of corruption.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

graft: Graft is the ongoing practice of using an official position to skim personal profit — kickbacks and payoffs flowing month after month. Corruption is the broader condition it belongs to: any dishonest abuse of entrusted power. Graft names the scheme; corruption names the rot in the institution.

bribery: Bribery is one specific, chargeable act: money or favors handed over to buy an official's decision. Corruption is the whole disease that bribery feeds — the general abuse of entrusted power for private gain. A single payment is bribery; a license office where payments are routine shows corruption.

dishonesty: Dishonesty is the everyday word for any lack of truthfulness or fair dealing — a shopper, a student, or a clerk can be dishonest. Corruption requires more: a position of entrusted power that is being traded away for private gain. Every corruption is dishonest; most dishonesty is not corruption.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

integrity: steadfast honesty and moral uprightness

honesty: truthful, fair conduct

Where it sits · how deep into crime the wrongdoing runs

favoritism → corruption → racketeering

favoritism vs. corruption: Favoritism — unfairly preferring one person over others — is troubling but not always illegal, while corruption involves genuinely dishonest abuse of power, usually for money.

racketeering vs. corruption: Racketeering goes beyond corruption: it means running an ongoing, organized criminal operation, not just misusing a single position of trust.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — cor-: thoroughly, altogether (assimilated form of Latin com-)

Root — rupt: to break (Latin rumpere, ruptus)

Suffix — -ion: forms nouns naming an act or its result

Put it together: Corruption is literally a 'thorough breaking' — moral character or public trust broken apart from within. The same rupt root powers interrupt, erupt, and rupture.

Use the root in a new word: rupture: The scandal caused a rupture between the senator and his oldest political allies.

Word Building

Word Choice

Formal / journalistic and legal

Corruption is specifically the abuse of entrusted power — an official trading the authority of their position for private gain, most often through bribes. Two words taught elsewhere in this unit are worth distinguishing by name: larceny is a particular crime of theft, and depravity describes a person's inner moral rottenness. Corruption, by contrast, always involves misusing a position of power.
